A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MDOT/PNCG research work. Their complete main texts, equations, algorithms, figures and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial revision.

before.justification: v2 reports original synthetic OT experiments and upsampled-MNIST benchmarking in Section 4 and Figures 1–4.

after.justification: v3 reports original ablations and benchmarking on MNIST, color transfer and DOTmark, including Figures 1–17 and Appendices C–F.

M1.justification: Within the retained MDOT framework, v3 adds temperature-dependent marginal smoothing and replaces the tau-scaled Hmin/gamma tolerance with a p-dependent rule. PNCG changes from the stated preconditioned Polak–Ribiere recurrence to Hestenes–Stiefel and corrects the descent-direction reset condition. The higher-order MDOT2 warm-start variant is removed; the first-order warm start and hybrid line search remain.

E1.justification: v3 extends MNIST evaluation from L1 to both L1 and squared-L2 costs, adds RGB color-transfer problems with uniform marginals, and evaluates ten DOTmark image datasets, including microscopy and classical images. Synthetic entropy-controlled problems remain, but their represented geometry and marginal construction change.

E2.justification: The main benchmarking adds evaluated APDAGD, AAM and Mirror Prox Sherman Optimized comparators to the retained Sinkhorn, MSK and Feydy methods. Projection comparisons add a stabilized diagonal-Hessian PNCG variant, while v2's vanilla-NCG comparison disappears. APDAMD and PDASMD are mentioned as attempted comparisons with omitted results.

E3.justification: Benchmarking changes from relative error to absolute primal optimality gap and introduces primitive-operation counting alongside wall-clock time. Main MDOT settings change from q=2 and initial inverse-temperature cap 64 to q=2^(1/3), gamma_i=16 and p=1.5. The main MNIST comparison uses 18 rather than 32 problems, and Feydy's fast/safe settings are replaced by an intermediate setting.

E4.justification: v3 substantially reworks warm-start testing and adds stopping-exponent sensitivity, diagonal-versus-Sinkhorn preconditioning, entropy-aware stopping, variable-versus-fixed smoothing, and overall problem-size scaling analyses. v2's higher-order warm-start, pseudo-condition-number and entropy-stratified projection analyses are removed rather than merely relocated.

E5.justification: v2's main MNIST benchmark reports medians with 90% confidence intervals; v3's corresponding main benchmark reports medians without intervals. v3 supplies 75% intervals for scaling and DOTmark results. These are changes in uncertainty reporting, without an explicit increase in seeded repeated runs.

E6.justification: v3 replaces the original synthetic and MNIST result curves and adds results across 24 benchmark settings. New findings include a nearly twofold PNCG benefit from variable smoothing in Figure 7 and measured problem-size scaling in Figure 5. Changed metrics, samples and solver settings prevent interpreting these as direct same-setting improvements over v2.

T1.justification: Several existing MD equivalence and error results are consolidated into Proposition 4.1, which also formalizes the role of inexact intermediate iterates. Remark 4.3 and Proposition 4.4 add a conditional, p-dependent Sinkhorn convergence analysis with proofs in Appendix A.3. v2's Hilbert-metric contraction proposition and higher-order finite-difference derivation are removed.

C1.justification: v3 adds a core contribution concerning the improved convergence rate of appropriately tuned Sinkhorn. Its abstract and conclusion broaden the empirical superiority claim to 24 problem sets and more solver families, and introduce explicit empirical accuracy and problem-size complexity claims. v2 primarily claims fast, precise MDOT/PNCG computation supported by synthetic and MNIST experiments.

C2.justification: The preconditioning explanation shifts from entropy-dependent pseudo-conditioning to numerical stability and local equivalence with diagonal-Hessian preconditioning. v3 also explains the benefits of variable smoothing and distinguishes uniform regularization-error bounds from faster asymptotic behavior, qualifying the benefits of larger p by sufficiently low temperatures.

D1.justification: v3 adds Appendix E with baseline implementation sources, reported PyTorch/NumPy equivalence checks, parameter ranges and numerical-failure thresholds. It also documents bilinear interpolation, generated color-image preparation and primitive-operation accounting. These substantially extend v2's implementation information; the GPU and 64-bit precision remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds targeted connections to exponential-convergence and stability work, including Weed and Eckstein–Nutz, plus Tang's sparse Newton method and DOTmark. The established positioning relative to epsilon-scaling, MSK, IPOT and other mirror-descent solvers largely remains. MSK's preprint-to-publication update concerns the same work.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method exposition and experimental narrative are extensively rewritten. Related work moves before the method, contributions become an explicit numbered list, and the appendices are reorganized around proofs, line search, targeted analyses, implementation details and benchmarking. This exceeds changes caused solely by added scientific content.

P2.justification: The original figures are substantially redesigned or replaced, and new ablation, scaling and DOTmark displays are added. Figure 4 changes from two relative-error panels to a four-panel absolute-gap/time comparison. Axes, legends, panel organization and captions change extensively, while algorithm blocks now share space with surrounding prose.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens the evidence behind the efficiency claims. The broader domains and cost functions, additional competitive baselines, parameter ablations and operation-count checks address the limited empirical support in v2's synthetic and single-MNIST benchmark evaluation. Appendix E also makes the comparisons easier to reproduce and assess. Removed entropy-specific analyses and missing uncertainty bars in the main benchmark are drawbacks, but the expanded controlled validation provides a clear substantial net gain.
